=== (3) HAZARDS / FRAGILE ASSUMPTIONS ===

HAZARD-1: The no-silent-bypass guarantee rests on the comptime `@compileError` in the RUNNERS block. It fires correctly today (verified by temporarily un-registering I7). But it only protects against a NEW `vb.Invariant` variant added WITHOUT a runner. If a future agent widens the `[DECLARED]` array manually (e.g. to `[DECLARED+1]`) or replaces the null-init + loop with a literal array, the gate is bypassed. The `comptime { if (RUNNERS.len != DECLARED) @compileError(...) }` assertion catches the width-mismatch case but not a literal-array rewrite that drops the null-check. Mitigation: the test `registry completeness: every declared invariant has a runner` pins `RUNNERS.len == DECLARED` at runtime, and the NAMES reflection test pins that every enum field name resolves — so a rewrite that decouples from the enum fails one of those.

HAZARD-2: The runners re-implement the module-status -> `vb.CheckStatus` mapping (mapTable/mapFix/mapI5) rather than importing `verify_battery.zig`'s mappers. `verify_battery.zig` is an exe root (private mappers, not a module), so vb_health cannot import it. The duplication is three 4-line switch fns. If a future module adds a NEW status variant (e.g. a `FixpointStatus.reference_disagreement`), the mapper here must be updated or that status will not round-trip. The per-module status enums are small and stable (pass/fail/not_applicable/err), so this is low-risk, but it IS a second source of truth for the mapping.

HAZARD-3: The health check's fixture is the 2×2 artifact (`artifacts/oracle-2x2.wzo`). The M9 mutant is format-agnostic (a stub returns `.skipped` regardless of artifact), so a 2×2 fixture is sufficient to exercise every runner. But it means the health check asserts 'every runner returns a real verdict ON 2×2', not 'on every goban'. A runner that stubs only at 4×4 would not be caught by THIS fixture. The M9 mutant as specified (an invariant that ALWAYS returns `.skipped`) is caught; a conditional stub is a different mutant. The brief scoped M9 as the unconditional stub, so this is in-spec.

HAZARD-4: `checkWith` takes `runners: []const RunnerFn` (a runtime slice) but indexes it with `f.value` (comptime int) inside an `inline for`. That compiles and runs, but it means the M9 mutant fixture copies the whole `[DECLARED]RunnerFn` array by value (`var mutant: [DECLARED]RunnerFn = RUNNERS;`) — a 12-pointer copy. Trivial at DECLARED=12; if the invariant set ever grows large, this remains O(DECLARED) per check call, which is fine.

WEAK-1: vb_health.zig is NOT wired into `build.zig` (the brief forbade editing build.zig). So `zig build test` does not run the 4 vb_health tests. The M9 kill test in vb_mutants.zig IS wired and DOES run. The DISCHARGE row (T348) / sprint console must add a `vb_health_tests` step to build.zig for the health check to run in CI. Until then, the health check is exercised only via the vb_mutants.zig M9 test (which imports vb_health) and by manual `zig test src/vb_health.zig`.

WEAK-2: I did not add a positive control that exercises the health check against a REAL `.skipped`-producing path in the live battery. The M9 fixture uses the exported `stubSkipped` runner. There is no live path today that returns `.skipped` (the module status enums lack it; `verify_battery.zig`'s `toExit` maps `.skipped => .pass` but nothing produces `.skipped`). So the check is calibrated against the synthetic stub only — which is exactly the M9 mutant as specified, so this is correct, but it means the check has no 'real' skipped to catch; its value is preventative.

WEAK-3: The `Verdict.statuses` array is filled but no test asserts the NON-skipped statuses are the expected real verdicts (e.g. that I2 returns `pass`, I3 returns `not-applicable`). The health check's job is the `.skipped` assertion, not re-verifying each invariant's verdict, so this is out of scope — but a future agent expecting `statuses` to be validated should know it is recorded, not asserted.
